evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep never framed the call length, promise of a dependable quote, or waited for customer agreement before proceeding.
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Name (Roger), phone (210-240-6901), email collected. Square footage (2400) and room layout discussed. No explicit moving date confirmed — customer said 'end of October, early November' but it was uncertain pending floor finisher.
evidence_quotes.walkthrough_branch: Rep correctly identified 2400 sq ft as 'a little bit larger' and offered virtual walkthrough via FaceTime link: 'They will probably do a virtual walkthrough just so they know exactly and then they'll just send you a link and then, be online with you like basically FaceTime.'
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Rep never asked about customer's concerns or what answers they wanted from the call. Jumped straight into confirming the service (floor furniture relocation) and logistics.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: No pricing anchor given. Rep mentioned hourly rate model and that costs are lower on Tuesdays–Thursdays but gave no range or estimate figure.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep never asked 'Would you like our help with your move?' or equivalent. Call ended with rep saying 'someone gives you a call right back' after putting customer on hold.

top_strength: Rep correctly routed a 2,400 sq ft move to a virtual walkthrough rather than attempting to quote on the phone, and collected all essential contact details (name, phone, email, address) cleanly to pass to the scheduling team.
coaching_note: Open with the quid pro quo framing ('10–15 minutes, walk away with a quote you can depend on, does that sound good?') before jumping into service confirmation, and always ask 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns about this move?' early to surface the customer's real priorities — even on a walkthrough-routed call, those insights guide the specialist.
